extraction_metadata.notes: Anthropic reported that Claude achieves a 28.2% hit rate in protein design — a frontier LLM successfully proposing proteins that experimentally validate. Directly relevant to the agentic-protein-discovery and natural-language-protein-design concept cards.

title: Claude achieves 28.2% hit rate in protein design
subtitle_or_tagline: A frontier language model crosses the experimental-validation threshold for de novo proteins
topic: Anthropic shared an update on Claude's protein design capabilities: the model achieves a 28.2% hit rate — meaning roughly 1 in 4 of its computationally designed proteins successfully express and fold as intended when tested experimentally. For context, historical de novo design hit rates were in the low single digits. A general-purpose language model (not a specialized structure-prediction pipeline) achieving this rate signals that biological reasoning is emerging as a capability of frontier LLMs rather than requiring bespoke architectures.

architecture.data_flow: design brief -> LLM reasoning -> candidate sequence -> experimental validation -> hit/miss feedback

workflow_steps: Step 1 - Specify target structure or function in natural language
Step 2 - Claude reasons about sequence constraints and proposes candidates
Step 3 - Candidates undergo experimental expression and folding tests
Step 4 - Hits validate at 28.2% rate (roughly 1 in 4 designs succeed)
Step 5 - Feedback loop improves future design rounds
key_claims: 28.2% experimental hit rate for Claude-designed proteins
General-purpose LLM, not a specialized protein-design architecture
Historical de novo design hit rates were in the low single digits
Biological reasoning is emerging as a frontier-LLM capability
Wet-lab validation, not just computational scoring
caveats_or_warnings: Hit rate does not specify binding affinity or functional potency of hits
Cost per candidate remains far higher than computational-only pipelines
28.2% is a headline number — per-family breakdown not yet public

citations.type: Anthropic update, shared by NC Frey

osiris_connection: A 28.2% hit rate is an empirical bound on design reliability — but nothing in the pipeline bounds the displacement between the designed sequence and its realized structure. OSIRIS's agentic-protein-discovery card argues that agent-designed proteins need Theorem 7 certificates: if each design iteration is a bounded update (norm-clamp on the embedding), the cumulative design drift is bounded by L*c, making 'the model proposes X, the lab confirms X' a certified rather than statistical claim. Claude's result shows the empirical loop works; OSIRIS's contribution is the mathematical version of the same guarantee.
